title: BATS sigma0 26.5 O2 loss (2014-2025) is a 0.075 kg/m3 AOU-profile shift, 0.7 of winter band lightening as in the North Pacific; with CMIP6 lightening it implies 60-70 umol/kg off California by 2050
abstract: Question: does the North Pacific density-shift relation for the sigma0 26.5 oxygen (O2) loss (AOU change = lighter shift of the AOU-density profile, 41-71% of winter outcrop lightening; sci:21ae52cf) also hold in the North Atlantic, and what does it imply for projections? Approach: we fitted the equivalent shift over sigma0 26.0-26.7 to BATS bottle data (431 cruises), WOD ship data and GLODAPv2.2023 in the western subtropical North Atlantic, with cruise bootstraps. We measured winter surface lightening with one metric in both basins: the January-April maximum surface sigma0 of WOA23 decades over the 26.2-26.8 outcrop band, plus an annual ship+Argo index. We tested six decades (1955-2022) and an annual out-of-sample test at BATS, and applied the relation to the band lightening of 30 CMIP6 models (SSP2-4.5, SSP5-8.5). Results: at BATS the shift was 0.075 kg/m3 (0.065-0.085, R2 0.94) for 2014-2025 vs 1984-1996 and none in 1997-2008; water on 26.5 became cooler and fresher. The NA band became lighter only in 2015-2022 (-0.105 kg/m3), matching the BATS timing. Transfer fraction f: 0.71 at BATS and 0.56-0.98 in the North Pacific with the same metric (annual indices: 0.92, 0.58-1.98, vs 0.41-0.71). Decadal shifts followed the surface in 4/4 decades for the NP 120-180 W band (f 0.73, r 0.98) and 3/4 at BATS (denser 1965-1984 gave negative shifts), but NP 1975-1984 densification gave no negative shift. The planned annual out-of-sample test at BATS failed (training years without signal; surrogate p 0.10). CMIP6 band lightening by 2041-2060 is 0.23-0.28 kg/m3 (NP) and 0.16-0.21 (NA); with f 0.84 the implied O2 on 26.5 off California is 72 (37-104) and 61 (20-96) umol/kg (1984-1996: 117.5), below 60 in 23-27 of 28 models near 2050; BATS stays above 175. Limitations: one NA site; projections extrapolate the relation 2-6 times beyond the observed range; asymmetric response to densification; one member per model; splice check set after seeing values.

Observed AOU change against sigma0 (solid) and the fitted shift of the reference profile (dashed) at BATS and in the North Pacific. Grey: fit range 26.0-26.7.

a: CMIP6 band winter surface density change (dots: models; bars: medians; stars: WOA23 observed). b: O2 on sigma0 26.5 that the observed shift relation implies (median, 10-90% of models), with the 60 umol/kg level.

citations.reason: We use its method, code, North Pacific shift values and reference profiles, and show that its density-shift relation also holds at BATS with a similar transfer fraction.
We adapt its WOA23/WOD surface index rules; the North Atlantic outcrop band also lost area, which supports outcrop loss as the common cause.
We use its 250 m BATS bracket rule and class-thickness predictor; the regional surface lightening after 2014 agrees with its finding that the 26.5 class stopped renewing.
We confirm the BATS oxygen loss on 26.5 (about 10-12 umol/kg) and express it as a density shift.
We use its WOA23 fetch script; because many CMIP6 models do not outcrop 26.5 in their own climate, we use only model density changes.
Its WOD extraction code (through sci:21ae52cf) is adapted here.
Model O2 comparison on 26.5; our CMIP6 results use surface density only.
Tracer-age evidence for ventilation change on 26.5 in both basins.
